answer: Each identity claims one vertex on a trellis ledger and locks an 80-credit bond. Its jobs carry a plume seal signed by the vertex key and epoch seed, so no seal moves to another vertex. Any peer may re-run a seal from the trellis record; failure forfeits the 80-credit bond to the challenger, while a false challenge burns the challenger's 40-credit stake. A rented key cannot mint a plume seal for the new seed, so vertex rental fails. The k-th fake needs a bond and a 60-credit fee, so 1,000 fakes burn 60,000 credits and lock 80,000. An honest agent pays 60 and recovers its bond after one epoch.
